observations.text: SP, due to an incorrect power and pursuit-curve technique as No2, did not maintain the Extended Trail position as described in the Techniques and Procedures Manual, allowing the cone to open past 60 degrees while the distance increased to about 1900 feet. The position was not re-established at any point of the maneuver sequence. The IP had to direct the rejoin and to fly part of the sequence, and the item could not be completed without assistance.

SP, due to a perceptual error in judging closure and lateral separation, did not respect the 500 feet safety bubble during the modified Barrel Roll, closing to an estimated 300 feet with the cone collapsing toward No1's 6 o'clock. SP constituted a threat for the formation during the maneuver. The IP intervened on the controls to open the separation and the maneuver was terminated.

SP maintained the Extended Trail position within the standards for the Training Section, but worked the outer edge of the permitted band, reaching about 1450 feet of distance and 60 degrees of cone on two occasions. Both deviations were recognized and corrected with delay, after the IP's verbal indications. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier recognition of the closure rate and independent correction of the cone are expected to improve.

SP maintained the Extended Trail position with the distance between 500 and 1200 feet and the cone between 25 and 55 degrees throughout the precision maneuvers, without stagnating in No1's 6 o'clock. The two minor deviations of the sortie were recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention and without any verbal indication. SP did not constitute a threat for the formation at any point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP held the Extended Trail position accurately and rapidly, keeping the distance between 500 and 1000 feet and the cone between 30 and 45 degrees through the modified Lazy 8 and the Cloverleaves. Power and pursuit-curve corrections were anticipated, with no IP intervention required. The 500 feet safety bubble was respected throughout the sortie. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Extended Trail position with negligible deviations, holding 600 to 850 feet of distance and a cone of 35 to 42 degrees through the full maneuver sequence within the 120 to 250 knots speed range. Energy and pursuit-curve management were exceptional for the Training Section, and the position never stagnated in No1's 6 o'clock. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, as Leader, due to abrupt control inputs and an unplanned entry airspeed, did not smoothly carry out the modified Chandelle within the 120 to 250 knots speed range, decelerating below 120 knots at the apex and exceeding 4 Gs in the recovery. The wingman was left beyond 1500 feet and outside the 20 to 60 degrees cone, with no correction called by the Leader. The IP had to direct the maneuver and to take over the formation calls. The item was not completed without assistance.

SP, as Leader, due to lack of awareness of the aircraft's position relative to the area boundary, did not maintain orientation within the assigned flight area during the Cloverleaves and did not control the wingman, who was left beyond the 1500 feet limit without any repositioning call. The maneuver sequence was continued toward the boundary without a corrective turn. The IP directed the recovery to the working area and executed part of the sequence.

SP, due to a late power reduction and an excessive lead pursuit at the entry of the modified Lazy 8, did not maintain the Extended Trail position, arriving at 1500 feet of distance with the cone at the 60 degrees limit. The position was re-established only after the IP's verbal indications. The deviation was recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to inadequate workload management inside the maneuver, did not avoid stagnation in No1's 6 o'clock, holding the cone at the 20 degrees limit through two consecutive reversals while the distance remained close to 1500 feet. Nose position and closure were not reassessed against the briefed cone. Return to the Extended Trail position followed only the IP's verbal indications, and the correction was applied with delay.

SP maintained the Extended Trail position within the standards for the Training Section, with the distance twice drifting to about 1200 feet and the cone to about 52 degrees during the Cloverleaves. Both deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner, without the IP's intervention and without any violation of the 500 feet safety bubble. Marginal performance for the Training Section - tighter control of the cone inside the reversals is expected to improve.

SP maintained the Extended Trail position accurately and rapidly, keeping the distance between 500 and 1000 feet and the cone between 30 and 45 degrees throughout the precision maneuvers. As Leader, the maneuvers were flown smoothly within the 120 to 250 knots speed range and within the assigned flight area, with the wingman controlled by timely calls. No IP verbal indication was required at any point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the Extended Trail position with negligible deviations, holding 600 to 900 feet of distance and a cone of 35 to 42 degrees through the modified Barrel Roll and the Cloverleaves. SP never stagnated in No1's 6 o'clock and at no time constituted a threat for the formation, with the 500 feet safety bubble respected by a wide margin. Position keeping and energy management were exceptional for the Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.
